analysis: The PR is docs-only. It modifies docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at line 3, plus a new paragraph at ~252-259 that is not within the supplied head excerpts) and docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (date bump plus a new paragraph at 784-790). The new text states that a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates destinations already available from host bytes, never evaluates or fences them, and so does not wait on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. It also says the import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. The only security-relevant aspect is a described change in the SSD prefix-cache staging path (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift), which falls under T-041 / TB-007 / A-001. The source change is not in the supplied evidence, so the claim cannot be verified here. The documented behavior affects availability and memory accounting (staging scratch is charged to the budget) and does not obviously change at-rest crypto, HMAC lookup naming, TTL, scope salting or authentication. T-041 mitigation text (reservation release paths, no persistent memory carve, transient staging reservation) stays consistent with the description. The next pass should confirm that the code change leaves staged host-byte destinations covered by the GlobalKVCacheBudget reservation and the staging release paths. It should also confirm that plaintext KV host buffers are not retained or zeroed unexpectedly. No new attack surface or threat-model invalidation is evidenced. Note: the inference.md excerpt covers only lines 406+, so the 252-259 addition was seen only via the patch excerpt.
